text: You can bring up to **68 semester credits** from another accredited university into an undergraduate program at Al Akhawayn University.
The catalog states that “for undergraduate programs, a maximum of 68 semester credits are transferable to AUI”[6].

(For reference, applicants must have at least 30 semester credits to be considered for admission, and if they have more than 60 credits of successful post‑secondary study they may be exempted from the Foundation Academic Studies (FAS) courses[4][6].)
Vous pouvez transférer des crédits à l’AUI selon votre niveau d’études :
**Programmes de premier cycle** : un maximum de **68 crédits semestriels** peuvent être transférés.
**Programmes de deuxième cycle (master, doctorat, etc.)** : un maximum de **12 crédits semestriels** peuvent être transférés.
Ces limites sont indiquées dans le catalogue académique de l’AUI [1].
Plagiarism at Al Akhawayn University is defined as any attempt by a student to present another person’s words, content, or ideas as their own.
This includes:
**Copying or paraphrasing text, images, ideas, or arguments** from another source without proper citation, footnote, or attribution, regardless of the length or formality of the work.
**Failing to distinguish** between what is original and what is borrowed, thereby misleading readers or viewers about the source of the material.
The university’s policy states that plagiarism is a “most serious offense” and that offenders can face severe sanctions, including possible expulsion.
The policy also notes that the university teaches students the formalities of properly crediting sources in several courses, and that faculty are expected to model and enforce these standards.

Selon le règlement de l’AUI, le plagiat est défini comme suit : « Toute tentative par un étudiant de présenter les mots, contenus ou idées d’une autre personne comme les siens est considérée par la faculté et l’administration comme une infraction grave. »
Les auteurs de plagiat sont passibles de sanctions sévères, notamment l’expulsion, la suspension ou l’échec à un cours [1].
To add or drop a course at Al Akhawayn University you should follow the university’s add/drop procedure:
**Check your standing**
You must be in good academic standing and have no holds on your account.
If you have an academic or other hold, you must go to the Registrar’s Office and complete an Add/Drop Form before you can start the process [1].
**Obtain permission**
You need permission from both your academic advisor and your school coordinator to add or drop a course (unless the course was listed as an “alternate course” on your registration form).
No one else (faculty, friends, or relatives) may add or drop courses on your behalf [1].
**Use the online add/drop system**
Students in good standing can add or drop courses online during the official add/drop period.
The add/drop is not official until all applicable tuition and fees have been paid [1].
**Know the add/drop period dates**
For the regular term, the add/drop window closes on the **4th class day**.
For summer sessions, it closes on the **2nd class day**.
Courses dropped within this period are not reflected on the academic record [4].
**After adding or dropping**
Ensure that any required tuition/fees are paid.
Verify that the changes appear on your academic record; if not, contact the Registrar’s Office.
If you are unsure about any part of the process or need clarification on dates for your specific term, it’s a good idea to double‑check with your academic advisor or the Registrar’s Office.
You can receive up to **three excused absences per semester** for university‑sponsored events such as sports, cultural activities, or other representative duties.
These absences must be approved in advance and will not count against your absence record [1].

To graduate with **Summa Cum Laude** (highest honors) at Al Akhawayn University, you must achieve a cumulative GPA in the range of **3.65 to 4.00**.
This threshold is specified in the academic catalog under the honors GPA scale [1].
Pour obtenir la mention **Summa Cum Laude** sur votre diplôme, vous devez avoir un **moyenne cumulative (CGPA) comprise entre 3,65 et 4,00** sur l’échelle de 4,0 de l’Université Akhawayn [7].
If your semester GPA falls between **1.5 and 1.99**, you will be placed on **academic probation** as an undergraduate student.
The policy states:
You are warned that your performance is below the required level.
In the following regular semester you may enroll in no more than **four courses (up to 13 semester hours)**.
To return to satisfactory standing you must achieve a semester GPA of **2.00 or higher** by the end of that semester.
Summer or inter‑session work does not count toward regaining satisfactory standing.
No notation of academic probation appears on your transcript.
If your GPA were below 1.5, you would be in unsatisfactory standing and would need to appeal for special permission.
The probation rules above apply only to the 1.5–1.99 range [8].
Si votre moyenne semestrielle (SGPA) se situe entre **1,50 et 1,99 sur 4,00**, votre aide financière est placée en **probation** :
Le financement est maintenu **conditionnellement**.
Vous devez obtenir une SGPA d’au moins **2,00 / 4,00** au semestre suivant pour que l’aide soit rétablie.
En dessous de 1,49 / 4,00, l’aide serait suspendue jusqu’à ce que vous atteigniez 2,00 / 4,00 ou plus.
Yes.
According to AUI’s repeat policy, an undergraduate may retake any course in which a **B‑ or lower** was earned.
A C‑ falls in that category, so you can retake the course [1].
For the cumulative GPA, the policy states that the **highest grade earned** in a repeated course is the one used in the GPA calculation and the course is counted only once toward credit [1].
So if you improve the grade on the retake, that new (higher) grade will replace the C‑ in your GPA.
Oui, vous pouvez reprendre ce cours.
Selon la politique de répétition de l’Université Al Akhawayn, un étudiant peut répéter tout cours dans lequel il a obtenu un **B‑ ou une note inférieure**.
Le cours que vous avez repris sera compté **une seule fois pour le crédit** et, pour le calcul du GPA cumulé, **seule la meilleure note obtenue** (la nouvelle ou l’ancienne) sera prise en compte.
En pratique, vous pourrez donc reprendre le cours et votre moyenne de licence sera calculée avec la note la plus élevée que vous avez obtenue sur ce cours [6].
A **W** on your transcript means that you withdrew from the course before the mid‑semester deadline.
The grade is recorded as a “withdrawal” and does **not** affect your GPA or academic standing.
If you withdraw after the mid‑semester cutoff, the instructor can assign a **WP** (withdrawal‑pass) or **WF** (withdrawal‑fail) instead of a plain W [2].
You can drop a course and still receive a W **until the last day of the add‑/drop period**.
For the 2024‑2025 academic year this date is **October 29**; after that date, instructors will determine a WP or WF grade [8].
La note **W** signifie **« withdrawal »** : l’étudiant a officiellement abandonné le cours (ou l’université) avant la date limite de retrait.
Le W n’apparaît pas dans le calcul du GPA et n’entraîne pas de pénalité académique tant qu’il est obtenu dans les délais prévus.
Pour un semestre régulier, jusqu’au **40ᵉ jour de classe** (c’est‑à‑dire avant le 40ᵉ jour de cours).
Pour un semestre d’été, jusqu’au **18ᵉ jour de classe**.
Après ces dates, l’instructeur doit attribuer soit un **WP** (retrait avec note passée au moment du retrait) soit un **WF** (retrait avec note échouée) ; le W ne sera plus possible [7] [8].
The conditions that a scholarship recipient must meet to **retain** their Al Akhawayn scholarship are set out in the university’s scholarship policy documents.
In short:

Category: **Graduate‑level scholarships**; Key Conditions for Renewal / Continuation: • Scholarship is valid for a maximum of **four enrolling semesters** (including one at the Language Center).  • To be renewed, the student must maintain a **Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) of at least 3.5**.  • An SGPA between **3.00 and 3.49** places the student on **probation**; failure to return to the required standing can trigger a **reduction or suspension** of the award.  • If a student receives a **W, WP, or WF** in all courses at the end of any semester, the scholarship is automatically **suspended** for the following semester.  • Graduate students who do **not qualify for a scholarship in their first semester** cannot apply for it in subsequent semesters.  • Graduate scholarship holders must also provide **unpaid part‑time service** (10 h per week, 160 h per semester) to the university, as assigned by the Financial Aid Office.

Category: **Undergraduate scholarships**; Key Conditions for Renewal / Continuation: • Scholarships are **non‑transferable** to other programs outside the school to which the recipient was initially admitted; however, a new candidate can change their chosen program before the first day of classes.  • Recipients must **confirm acceptance** of the award and its renewal policy by paying the required **scholarship deposit** before the deadline.  • Undergraduate scholarship holders must maintain good academic standing (the policy specifies that the **summer session GPA is not counted** for probation, suspension, or reinstatement).

Category: **General requirements**; Key Conditions for Renewal / Continuation: • Students must **confirm acceptance** of the scholarship by paying any deposit required by the Admissions or Financial Aid Office.  • For graduate scholarships, a **non‑refundable advance of 10 000 MAD** must be paid within the set deadline to confirm acceptance.
In practice, to keep a scholarship you need to:
**Maintain the required GPA** (≥ 3.5 for graduate students, and good academic standing for undergraduates).
**Avoid probation or suspension** by meeting the GPA threshold and by not receiving only withdrawals/failed grades.
**Fulfil service obligations** (10 h/week for graduate scholarship holders).
**Pay any required deposits or fees** to confirm acceptance and renewal.
If any of these conditions are not met, the scholarship may be **reduced, placed on probation, or suspended** according to the university’s policy.
It is advisable to discuss your specific situation with an academic advisor to confirm how the rules apply to your program.

To register for **ACC 2302 — Accounting Principles II**, you must first complete its direct prerequisite and any courses that are required by that prerequisite.
The full prerequisite chain is:
**ACC 2302** – requires **ACC 2301**[1].
**MTH 1303** – Calculus I: Differential and Integral Calculus (no further prerequisites listed)[1].
**MTH 1304** – Discrete Mathematics for Engineers (no further prerequisites listed)[1].
**MTH 1305** – referenced in the catalog but its description and prerequisites are not provided in the available documents[1].
So, before taking ACC 2302 you need to have completed ACC 2301, and for that you must have taken at least one of MTH 1303, MTH 1304, or MTH 1305.
If you’re unsure about MTH 1305 or want to confirm the exact sequence for your program, it’s a good idea to check with an academic advisor.
Pour vous inscrire à **ACC 2302 : Accounting Principles II**, vous devez d’abord avoir terminé **ACC 2301 : Accounting Principles I**.
La chaîne de prérequis est la suivante :
**ACC 2301** – prérequis : MTH 1305, ou MTH 1303, ou MTH 1304 [1]
**MTH 1303** : Calculus I : Differential and Integral Calculus – aucun prérequis indiqué [1]
**MTH 1304** : Discrete Mathematics for Engineers – aucun prérequis indiqué [1]
**MTH 1305** – référencé mais sans description détaillée dans le catalogue, donc aucune information supplémentaire disponible [1]
En pratique, vous devez donc :
Suivre **ACC 2301**.
Avant ACC 2301, choisir **au moins l’un** des cours de mathématiques suivants : **MTH 1305, MTH 1303 ou MTH 1304**.
Les cours MTH 1303 et MTH 1304 n’ont pas de prérequis supplémentaires.
MTH 1305 est mentionné mais son contenu exact n’est pas fourni dans le catalogue.
Il est recommandé de vérifier ces prérequis avec un conseiller académique, surtout si votre parcours académique implique des exigences spécifiques à votre faculté.

Al Akhawayn University offers several merit‑based scholarship programmes that are open to international students.
The main options are:

Scholarship: **AUI Scholarship for New Students**; Who can apply: Fresh‑enrolled undergraduates (including international candidates); What it covers: 10 %–60 % of tuition (and sometimes additional costs); Key points: Merit‑based – no financial need considered. Eligibility requires a high academic profile (e.g., a Moroccan or French baccalaureate with a “mention Bien”, an American baccalaureate with an SGPA ≥ 3.50/4.00, or comparable scores from other systems) plus a strong General Admission Test score, a favorable scholarship interview, and an essay. The award is usually only for the Fall session.  [2]

Scholarship: **AUI Scholarship for Continuing Students**; Who can apply: Undergraduate and graduate students already enrolled at AUI; What it covers: 10 %–60 % of tuition; Key points: Merit‑based and renewable each semester.  Students must maintain a minimum GPA (≥ 3.00/4.00 for undergrads, ≥ 3.50/4.00 for graduates) and comply with scholarship‑renewal criteria such as campus employment restrictions.  [3]

Scholarship: **AUI External Scholarship**; Who can apply: Graduate students (including international PhD/MA candidates); What it covers: Full external scholarships that cover tuition and sometimes living expenses; Key points: Students must meet AUI’s renewal criteria (≥ 3.00/4.00 for undergrads, ≥ 3.50/4.00 for graduates).  External scholarships cannot be combined with other AUI discounts.  [3]

Scholarship: **Alumni’s Child Discount**; Who can apply: International students who are children of AUI alumni; What it covers: Up to 10 000 MAD off tuition; Key points: This is a discount rather than a scholarship and cannot be combined with any other scholarship or discount.  [5]
**Undergraduates** – complete the online scholarship application before the Fall deadline (usually 31 May for Fall, 31 Oct for Spring).
**Graduates** – download and submit the Graduate Scholarship Form before the relevant deadline.
The same academic‑profile requirements that apply to Moroccan students apply to international students.
In short, you need a high‑grade secondary‑school diploma (or equivalent) and a strong General Admission Test score, plus a positive interview and essay.
The scholarships are awarded purely on merit, not on financial need [2].
If you’re interested in a specific scholarship or want to confirm your eligibility, it’s a good idea to speak with the Office of International Programs or an academic advisor.

It is listed in the catalog as part of the general‑education requirements for students minoring in Business Administration (SSAH) and is referenced in the course list for that minor [2][3].
